documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Visit (received)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN — prenatal visit 1/26/2026, copy to primary care.

34-year-old G4P2013 at 33w0d, singleton. Background: peripartum cardiomyopathy after her 2023 delivery, recovered; vasa previa with emergency cesarean for twins in 2/2025; generalized anxiety disorder; impaired glucose tolerance; postpartum thyroiditis in 2024.

She came today mainly to ask that this baby be delivered by planned cesarean. She describes a great deal of fear about going through labor and a vaginal birth this time — much more than with her first, which was an easy term vaginal delivery of a 3500 g baby. No bleeding, no fluid leaking, no contractions. This pregnancy has been unremarkable: glucose testing normal, blood pressures normal with no gestational hypertension.

Meds: carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, sertraline 50 mg daily, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa drugs, latex.

Exam: BP 120/78, HR 82. Nonstress test reactive and reassuring, no decelerations.

Counseling: with one prior low transverse cesarean she is a candidate for either a trial of labor after cesarean or a planned repeat cesarean. We went through the benefits and risks of each for this pregnancy and for future ones. She has thought about it carefully and is firm in choosing a repeat cesarean; her anxiety is a legitimate part of that decision.

Plan: planned repeat cesarean at 39 weeks — booked 3/9/2026. Anesthesia and cardiology aware; latex-free. Weekly visits from 36 weeks. Encouraged her to talk with her PCP about anxiety support in the meantime.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit — Anxiety
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit. 34 weeks. OB note from 1/26 reviewed — repeat cesarean booked 3/9.

S: Anxiety higher the last month. Lies awake running through what happened with the twins (the bleeding, the rush to the OR), and fears labor. Feels a lot calmer since the c-section date was set. Sleeping 5-6 h. No panic attacks. Mood otherwise ok, still enjoying the kids and her class. No SI. Taking sertraline 50 daily.
GAD-7 12.

O: On video, tearful at moments, organized, good insight.

A/P: GAD with a flare in late pregnancy, tied to the prior emergency delivery and fear of labor.
- Offered a sertraline increase to 100 mg; she prefers to stay at 50 mg for the last weeks and revisit after delivery. Reasonable.
- Talked through what the planned delivery will look like vs last time; she found that helpful.
- Check-in by text weekly; postpartum visit with me 2-3 weeks after delivery, with mood screening.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary (received)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital — obstetric discharge summary.
Admitted 3/9/2026, discharged 3/11/2026.

Indication: planned repeat cesarean at 39w0d, patient choice after counseling, one prior cesarean.
Procedure 3/9/2026: repeat low transverse cesarean under spinal anesthesia, latex-free. Liveborn infant, vigorous, well, rooming in.

Course: uncomplicated. No heart failure symptoms; euvolemic; cardiology consulted. Breastfeeding established.

Discharge medications:
- enalapril 10 mg twice daily — restarted postpartum per cardiology
- carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily
- sertraline 50 mg daily
- prenatal vitamin daily
- oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 every 6 hours as needed for severe pain, #10
Allergies: sulfa drugs, latex.

Follow-up: cardiology echo in ~6 weeks; OB at 6 weeks; primary care in 2 weeks.

documents.title: Transitional Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home 3/11 after planned repeat c-section. "So much calmer than last time." Baby well, nursing going ok. Pain controlled, oxycodone twice total. Taking enalapril 10 bid, carvedilol, sertraline, PNV. No SOB, no orthopnea, no leg swelling. Incision dry. Booked PCP 3/26.

documents.title: Office Visit — Postpartum
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
2.5 weeks after planned repeat c-section (3/9). Baby well, here in a carrier.

S: Feels good, recovery easier than with the twins. Off oxycodone. Breastfeeding. No dyspnea, orthopnea or edema. Back on enalapril 10 bid since delivery; carvedilol 6.25 bid; sertraline 50; PNV. Anxiety settled a lot after the delivery — GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 3. Doesn't want to change sertraline now.

O: Vitals as charted, weight 71 kg. Heart regular, no gallop. Lungs clear. Incision healing well. No edema, calves soft.

A/P:
1. Postpartum after repeat cesarean — doing well. CBC.
2. PPCM recovered — back on enalapril; BMP today. Cardiology echo 4/20.
3. IGT — restart metformin discussion at the May visit with A1c (A1c too early now after delivery).
4. Postpartum thyroiditis history — TSH at the May visit, sooner for palpitations, weight loss or fatigue out of proportion.
5. GAD — improved; recheck in May.

reports.text: Comparison 8/11/2025. Normal LV size and wall motion. LVEF 55%. Normal RV size and function. Valves structurally normal. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up (received)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology 4/20/2026, six weeks after repeat cesarean.

Well, no HF symptoms. Euvolemic. Echo LVEF 55%, unchanged.

PPCM, recovered and stable through two further pregnancies.
Plan: continue enalapril 10 mg BID and carvedilol 6.25 mg BID while breastfeeding and for now; we will discuss a supervised taper next year. Echo in 12 months. Allergies: sulfa, latex.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Obstetrics Postpartum Visit (received)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN — postpartum visit 4/23/2026, 6 weeks after repeat cesarean.

Recovering well. Breastfeeding. Mood good. No bleeding now. Incision healed. Pelvic exam normal. Pap with HPV collected (overdue since 2025) — result: negative.

Meds: enalapril 10 mg BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, sertraline 50 mg daily, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.
Return for annual GYN care; glucose follow-up with PCP.
